transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date: 2026-06-11
- Start: 15:00 UTC
- Duration: ~52 minutes
- Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Luca (Redwood SE), Priya (Helix), Daniel (Helix), Aisha (Helix), Tom (Helix)

Summary (auto-gen, may be rough):
Redwood overview, mapping playbook for OpenAI/Anthropic/Together endpoints to Redwood API, console walkthrough highlights (Optimize suggestions, console rollouts), security checklist, initial perf bench plan.

Topics:
- Why swap and success criteria
- API parity and request/response mapping
- Latency vs. cost / batching / quantization
- Dedicated vs hosted vs private deployment for data residency
- Security: SOC2, SSO, KMS, audit logs
- Next steps and benchmarks

Transcript body:
[00:00] Maya: hey everyone thanks for joining, um we'll do a quick intro then jump into the mapping playbook. can you hear me okay?
[00:12] Priya: yes loud and clear, thanks, I'm Priya, we run the ML infra at Helix, looking to consolidate vendors and reduce token cost while keeping our 95pct latency targets.
[00:20] Daniel: daniel here, platform lead, also want to understand what breaks in our current pipelines when swapping providers.
[00:28] Maya: perfect. Luca, want to do the tech overview?
[00:31] Luca: sure. quick context: Redwood exposes a single API for text generation, chat, embeddings. for migrations we map provider models and common param semantics. we do continuous batching, prefix/KV caching — sometimes the transcript says KV cash — but basically the kv cache manages chat state.
[00:54] Priya: quick Q — we use OpenAI for chat completions and Anthropic for some assistant models, plus Together for a couple private endpoints. will all of that map cleanly?
[01:06] Luca: high level yes, but there are three classes: direct parity, shim-needed, and behavior-different. direct parity is usually for single-turn generation. shim-needed covers things like role-system-preservation and function calling differences. behavior-different is mostly due to model architecture and tokenization differences; we give quantization and prompt-tuning suggestions.
[01:28] Tom: interjection — what about streaming? we need server-sent events for our UI.
[01:33] Maya: yes streaming is supported, we have examples in the console and SDK. there's small latency overhead depending on batch window, which Luca will cover.
[01:40] [Speaker 1]: (mumbles)
[01:44] Luca: on latency vs cost: obvious tradeoff — dedicated pools give predictable p95 latency; hosted is cheaper at low scale but variable. our Optimize tool will recommend batching and cache configs per workload to hit cost targets. for example, if you have many short messages, tiny batch windows plus prefix caching works well.
[02:10] Priya: our SLO is 350ms p95 for single-turn assistant prompts at 2k qps. is dedicated the only way?
[02:20] Luca: not necessarily. we can get there with hosted if you provision high-tier capacity and use KV caching aggressively, but predictable p95 at that load is usually a dedicated contract. also our dedicated instances run on reserved GPU pools and provide SLA-backed latency.
[02:36] Aisha: security side — we need KMS integration, enterprise KMS or HSM, and audit logs. also data residency in eu-west. can you support customer-managed keys and per-request audit trails?
[02:50] Maya: yes, private and dedicated both support customer KMS. we log request metadata and can push audit logs to your SIEM. Luca, quick on SAML/SSO?
[03:00] Luca: SAML/Sso yes, RBAC via console, and we do token-level cost traces in the Console. for KMS we have a guides folder, but I'll follow up with the integration doc.
[03:12] Daniel: what about model fallback? our handling needs graceful degradation if a variant isn't available.
[03:18] Luca: auto-fallback to compatible model variants by routing policy is built in — you can set fallbacks by latency or cost. we also support A/B rollouts and manual canary.
[03:30] Priya: on the mapping, show us a concrete example — say OpenAI chat endpoint with function calling to Redwood equivalent.
[03:40] Maya: good — Luca, can you pull up the mapping doc?
[03:44] Luca: (screen share noise) here's an example. OpenAI's chat.completions with functions -> Redwood's chat endpoint with function schema in a JSON field. slight naming diffs: "messages" stays, "role":"system" mapping is preserved but we recommend using explicit system prefixes for parity. also watch out for Together's tokenization differences — sometimes prompt windows shift by a token.
[04:12] Tom: will our existing embeddings index break? we pre-compute embeddings with Together's ada-variant.
[04:20] Luca: embeddings are usually compatible but distances shift; we recommend a short reindex or hybrid approach: dual-write for a week to compare. our Optimize will suggest quantization and embedding model choices.
[04:35] Priya: noise: (laugh) we hate reindexing. can you quantify expected drift?
[04:40] Luca: typical drift is 2–6% in similarity scores depending on models; in practice, downstream retrieval recall impacts are small but worth validating via a smoke test.
[04:52] Maya: also note cost differentials — our price sheet will show per-token and peak capacity tiers; you'll likely see 20–40% unit cost savings after batching and caching for chat-heavy workloads.
[05:10] Daniel: can we have a quick console tour — where do we configure batching and see Optimize suggestions?
[05:16] Maya: sure, we'll switch to the console. (brief pause) this is the routes page, you can set per-route policies; here's Optimize which surfaces batch window recommendations, cache TTL, and suggested quantization for the model family. you can simulate cost impact before applying.
[05:44] Priya: ok cool. question on private deployment — if we want on-prem for regulated data, how long to stand that up?
[05:52] Luca: typical private deployment is 6–10 weeks depending on networking and HSM access; we do a split plan: small pilot in a VPC first then an on-prem package if needed.
[06:05] Aisha: SSO and audit logs must meet our infosec checklist — SOC2 + ISO are table stakes, but do you support log forwarding to our Splunk?
[06:14] Luca: yes, we support log forwarding via syslog/S3 and have event schemas for SIEM integration. we'll attach our compliance pack.
[06:26] Maya: circling back: success criteria — Priya, what would make this a win for Helix?
[06:31] Priya: parity on core intents, <10% regression on downstream metrics, cost reduction, and no security gaps. timeline is Q3 pilot.
[06:40] Maya: good. for the pilot we propose 2-week functional parity run, and a 2-week perf bench with production traces. we'll need sample traffic and a list of top 200 prompts.
[06:52] Daniel: we can do that. we'll also want to capture tail latency at 99pct for the perf run.
[06:58] Luca: noted. on the bench methodology: short-run synthetic (1h) then long-run production replay (24–72h) to catch cache/kv warmup and batching effects. we can help run both.
[07:12] Tom: question about feature flags — if we flip to Redwood, how do we revert?
[07:18] Maya: we recommend adapter-layer toggles in your routing, plus Redwood's canary rollouts so you can fall back. we'll provide a client shim initially to reduce lift.
[07:28] Priya: any gotchas on token counting differences? our billing dashboards must align.
[07:34] Luca: yes tokenization differences exist. we provide token-mapping heuristics and a token-translation script. also Console shows token-level breakdowns per request to reconcile billing.
[07:48] Aisha: legal/procurement — will we need new contracts for dedicated vs hosted?
[07:53] Maya: yes, dedicated is contract-based with capacity commitments; hosted can be on usage pricing. legal team will provide templates.
[08:00] (short cross talk)
[08:07] Maya: ok quick demo in the console of an adapter example...
[08:12] Luca: here's an example adapter snippet: replace openai.ChatCompletion.create with redwood.chat.create, map messages, pass functions as schema. small code sample in the migration repo we'll send.
[08:30] Priya: ask — can you handle multimodal attachments later? we have a roadmap to add images.
[08:36] Luca: we have beta multimodal support; we'll add that to the timeline.
[08:40] Maya: time check, we're at 30 minutes, want to make sure security questions are answered and recap next steps.
[08:47] Aisha: quick thing — retention settings, can we set per-route data retention and delete requests after N days?
[08:54] Luca: yes, per-route retention is configurable and deletions can be enforced; we also support data anonymization hooks.
[09:03] Priya: last Q — do you offer a white-glove migration service?
[09:08] Maya: yes, for enterprise we offer migration services, benching support, and a dedicated solutions engineer during the pilot. cost and scope vary.
[09:18] Daniel: good. let's confirm timeline and roles.
[09:22] Maya: recap next steps: Maya sends price + mapping examples, Luca sends security/KMS + SAML guides, Helix shares sample traffic and latency targets. schedule bench slots — Daniel, what days next week look good?
[09:36] Daniel: Tue/Thu morning PT are best.
[09:40] Maya: great. any other questions?
[09:43] (silence)
[09:46] Maya: thank you everyone, we'll follow up with notes and artifacts.
[09:50] Priya: thanks all.
